title: Pizarro to Cajamarca and Cusco, 1531–33
summary: Pizarro sailed from Panama at the end of 1530 or in January 1531 with about 180 men and 27 horses, landed on the Ecuadorian coast and made his way to Tumbes, then inland. At Cajamarca on 16 November 1532 his men ambushed and took the Sapa Inca Atahualpa, killing thousands of his unarmed escort. Atahualpa filled a room with gold for his ransom and was executed in 1533, and the Spanish took Cusco in November.

events.label: Cajamarca: Atahualpa taken
events.text: Atahualpa came into the square with thousands of unarmed attendants, and the Spanish fired and charged from the buildings. The Inca escort was killed, and Atahualpa was taken. The room he offered to fill with gold, 22 by 17 feet, was filled to a line as high as he could reach.

events.label: Cusco taken
events.text: The Spanish took the Inca capital, with the help of many Indigenous allies, installed Manco Inca, a brother of Atahualpa, as a puppet, and founded their Spanish city. Manco rose against them in 1536.
